title: A python script that runs a subprocess with a list argv and no shell is read as text by the other-checkout guard
why: Under the 08:43 CST Nov 8 ruling, a script that imports subprocess makes its quoted arguments shell text. So a judge script that runs `subprocess.run([sys.executable, guard])` with a quoted command still raises the other-checkout false alarm, the original 12:25-12:26 incident (lane guard-relative-write-escape, session_013NEJKzJxDxuXzuwNe7fhYn, 09:05 CST Nov 8).
note: Fix: extend python_body_is_text (home of step other-checkout-heredoc-text, #1906) to treat a subprocess call as text when its argv is a list literal whose first element is not a literal shell (sh, bash, zsh and the like) and it has no shell=True. Held out of guard-quoted-args-data to keep that branch inside the review cap. Merge after #1906. Done check: a red test where that judge script passes, while a list argv that starts with bash, or shell=True, is still read as shell. Filed by triage 09:07 CST Nov 8. Doing 10:14 CST Nov 8: built as draft #2125 (head 96fb29597, merge after #1906), review round 1, lane other-checkout-cp-own. Rule narrowed: the first argv element must be python or sys.executable.
